chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Misma' ibn Abdul Malik, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him).

Regarding a man who was in Ihram inside the Haram, he shot a prey outside the Haram and killed it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the compensation, because the injury came to it from the Haram.'

He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who shot a prey outside the Haram in the unrestricted area (Hill). So the prey survived until it entered the Haram. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Its flesh is prohibited, like the dead meat.'

key_terms.الْحِلّ: The unrestricted area outside the Sanctuary

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on hunting prey that dies inside the Haram if shot from outside?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'cause and effect' in hunting jurisprudence, distinguishing between the location of the shot and the location of death. It establishes that if the act of hunting originates within the sanctuary, the prey requires expiation (kaffarah) even if killed outside; conversely, if the prey enters the sanctuary after being shot, its meat becomes prohibited (haram) like carrion, reflecting the sanctity of the space itself. This ruling underscores the unique legal status of the Haram as a zone where specific violations carry distinct spiritual and material consequences.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziiyad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man, not in Ihram, being inside the Al-Harram, pelts a prey outside from the Al-Harram, so he kills it. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him is the compensation, because the injury came to it from the Al-Harram’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who pelted a prey outside from the Al-Harram in the unrestricted area. So the prey survives until it enters the Al-Harram. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Its flesh is prohibited like the dead’.
en.sarwar: 14. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad am Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father all from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from Misma’ ibn ‘ Abd al-Malik who has said the following:

“About a man who, is not in the state of Ihram, shoots from inside of al-Haram (the sacred area) a prey outside of al-Haram (the sacred area) and kills it, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘There is ransom on him because calamity came upon the bird from al-Haram (the sacred area).

5 I asked him (the Imam), about a man who shoots a prey outside al-Haram (the sacred area) in non-al- Haram (the sacred area) and it moves until it enters al-Haram (the sacred area). He (the Imam) said, ‘Its meat is prohibited for him like a dead animal’s.
